newsitem.title: USA: Reebok not to make share repurchases.
newsitem.headline: Reebok not to make share repurchases.

text.p: Reebok International Inc Chief Financial Officer Kenneth Watchmaker said the company will not make share repurchases in the near-term, but will pay down debt instead.
"We don't expect to be making any open market share repurchases in the near-term," Watchmaker told analysts and reporters on a telephone conference call.

He also said that SG&A expenses this year will rise over last year's levels, due in part to new product development centers to be opened in Taiwan and China, and expanded design and engineering development in the United States.

"Looking ahead to the remainder of 1997, we expect our full year SG&A spending to increase versus 1996, primarily due to increases in product development and retail operating expenses," Watchmaker said.
However, as a percentage of sales, SG&A spending ratios should improve this year over last, he said.
"We have squeezed about all we can at this time out of infrastructure type expenses," he added.
Watchmaker said the strong U.S. dollar, which negatively impacted its reported international sales and margins, will continue to impact this year's comparisons over last year.
"We are experiencing more margin pressure than we anticipated due to the stronger U.S. dollar," Watchmaker said.

Bob Meers, head of the Reebok brand, said the 0.3 percent year-over-year upturn in North American footwear sales after a year of declining quarterly sales reflects the company's efforts to turn the business around.
"We've turned the corner on our North American footwear business," he said.

The company plans to further strengthen the brand by reducing the sale of lower-priced shoes to volume retailers, while increasing sales to athletic specialty stores of higher-priced shoes, he said. The company thereby raises the average price of its shoes.
Meers said Reebok will launch a coordinated global marketing campaign in the spring of 1998 to boost the brand image.
